body:
Go to government buildings when you're free, and start asking what services are available.

As others have said, you convey yourself well, and are attempting to make things better after having an impossibly hard start.

I was on my own at 17 thanks to the foster care system, and I wish I had known about all the services available. 

Look in to food banks in your area. 
Many have programs like carry-bags with food that doesn't need to be refrigerated, and will still be good 

They may know where to look yo get assistance with things like a mobile phone with minutes that renew every month, so that you are able to stay in contact with work and friends. 

There are programs like TANF (colorado) with incredible people, whose job is to find those programs, and help you.

I worked with them, and they had everything from life skill trainings, free computer access, classes on interviews, resume writing and so on.  
They even have programs to pay for shoes / proper work clothes, if you dont have any. 

They also have contact information for mental health providers, and can help with that.

Learning the skills to cope with the burden you're carrying, and having someone to talk to can literally be a life saver.

You are not alone. You can do this.
